messages.subject: CODEX for Mus Musculus
parts:
Hi Yuchao,

I'm currently planning to use CODEX for data from mouse. I managed to adapt the getgc() code so that it works with the BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10 package, that contains the mm10 genome sequence.
Now I'm stuck with the precomputed mapability. Can you reveal how you calculated mapability for the human genome? I would like to adapt it for mouse. I could then send you the modified code, for a possible integration into CODEX.

Best and let me know what you think.
Jens

messages.author: 94ec915e8ce36448
messages.subject: Re: CODEX for Mus Musculus
parts:
Hi Jens,

Apology for my late reply--just got back from a workshop. Attached is the code that I used to generate mappability for human. I am sure you can easily adapt it to the mouse genome. Note that the code has not been optimized and you might need parallel computing to run it efficiently. In CODEX, the mappability is pre-computed and stored for exonic regions.

We will include BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10 as a dependent package and update CODEX to be suited for mouse genome in the next version. Thanks very much for pointing this out.

Cheers,
Yuchao

--
Yuchao Jiang (yuc...@mail.med.upenn.edu)
PhD student in Genomics and Computational Biology
University of Pennsylvania

messages.author: 94ec915e8ce36448
messages.subject: Re: CODEX for Mus Musculus
parts:
Hi Jens,

(1) It’s better if you use your designed targets. What’s done by CODEX by default is that we overlap the input targets with the pre-stored targets whose mappabilities are already calculated. This dramatically reduces the computation time. Also the mappability computation is only for the QC procedure where we remove regions of the genome that are for example, segmental duplication regions.

(2) The script I gave you is only for computing mappability for chr22. The brief idea is that we generate consecutive pseudo-reads covering the exonic regions in chr22 and map them back to the entire genome (note that here it’s not limited to chr22 only as a read might be mapped to multiple different regions in the genome). You will have to run for each chromosome of the mouse. Again, the code isn’t optimized as we didn’t include that in the package however you can run each target from each chromosome in parallel.

Hope that this clarifies,
Yuchao
